# 5 · Intune Device Writeback (Entra / Graph) {.unnumbered}

This is the first of the two live write planes. For **Entra-joined client
devices**, OrgPath facets are written to the device object's
`onPremisesExtensionAttributes` via Microsoft Graph. Intune dynamic groups then
target those attributes — that is how OrgPath "drives Intune."

CLI: `uiao orgtree assess --write` · Adapter:
`uiao.adapters.entra_device_orgpath.EntraDeviceOrgPathAdapter` · Transport:
`uiao.adapters.graph_transport.GraphTransport`.

::: {.callout-note}
## Writeback ≠ profile authoring

This writes OrgPath *facet values* onto device objects. Assigning Intune
*configuration profiles / compliance policies* to the resulting dynamic groups
is a separate concern — its targeting model is canon (UIAO_011), but the
authoring adapter is a **reserved** slot, not part of this path. See Guide 7.
:::

## 5.1 Disposition decides the plane

Each device record carries a **disposition** that routes its write:

| Disposition | Plane | Transport |
|---|---|---|
| `ENTRA-DEVICE` | entra | Microsoft Graph (this guide) |
| `ARC-SERVER`, `STAY-AD-DEPENDENCY`, `MANAGED-IDENTITY-CANDIDATE` | arm | Azure Resource Manager (Guide 6) |
| `STAY-AD-DC`, `DECOMMISSION` | skip | No write attempted |

Set `disposition` on each record in your device export (defaults to
`ENTRA-DEVICE` if absent). This guide covers `ENTRA-DEVICE`.

## 5.2 What gets written

For an `ENTRA-DEVICE`, the adapter batches all derived facets into **one**
Graph PATCH on the device:

```
PATCH /devices/{device_id}
{
  "onPremisesExtensionAttributes": {
    "extensionAttribute1": "EASTUS",     # region
    "extensionAttribute2": "IT",         # department
    "extensionAttribute4": "Engineer",   # role
    ...                                   # up to 10 named facets
  }
}
```

Reserved facets (slots 11–15) and any value that would land as drift are
**skipped** — the adapter never writes a value the engine would immediately
flag.

## 5.3 Dry-run first (always)

`--write` defaults to dry-run: it **plans** the per-facet writes and dispatches
nothing. No credentials required.

```bash
uiao orgtree assess \
  --from-export ad-devices.json \
  --target-type device \
  --write
```

```
Device writes — dry_run=True, cloud=commercial
  Planned : 870
  Sent    : 0
  Skipped : 870        # dry-run sends nothing
```

Review the plan: `Planned` is the per-facet operation count across all
`ENTRA-DEVICE` records. If that number and the per-device facet spread look
right, proceed.

## 5.4 Go live

Add `--no-dry-run`. This requires `UIAO_ENTRA_*` credentials (Guide 1) and the
`[api]` extra. For GCC-Moderate keep `--cloud commercial`:

```bash
uiao orgtree assess \
  --from-export ad-devices.json \
  --target-type device \
  --write --no-dry-run \
  --cloud commercial
```

```
Device writes — dry_run=False, cloud=commercial
  Planned : 870
  Sent    : 860
  Skipped : 0
  Errors  : 10
```

The CLI builds a `GraphTransport` from the environment, acquiring a
**Graph-audience** token for the selected cloud (commercial Graph =
`graph.microsoft.com`, which is correct for GCC-Moderate). Each `ENTRA-DEVICE`
becomes one batched PATCH.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Pilot discipline

Smoke-test on a **single device** before the fleet: export one record, run the
dry-run, then `--no-dry-run`, then confirm in the Entra portal that
`extensionAttribute1..10` carry the expected values. Only then widen scope.
:::

## 5.5 Failure modes

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `--no-dry-run requires UIAO_ENTRA_* credentials` then exit 1 | Env vars unset / `[api]` extra missing | Set `UIAO_ENTRA_*`; `pip install "uiao[api]"` |
| HTTP 401 on PATCH | Missing admin consent for `Device.ReadWrite.All`, or wrong `--cloud` | Grant + consent the Graph app permission; match `--cloud` to the tenant |
| HTTP 403 on PATCH | App lacks rights on the target object | Confirm application permission scope and consent |
| Device facets blank after write | Values skipped as drift, or reserved facets | Run `govern` (Guide 4); resolve P2 Value drift; reserved slots aren't written |
| `--write applies only to device assignments` | `--target-type` not `device` | Add `--target-type device` |
| Per-op errors in the `Errors` count | Transient Graph errors / throttling on specific devices | Re-run; the plan is idempotent (PATCH of the same values is a no-op) |

## 5.6 Re-running is safe

The write is an idempotent PATCH of the desired facet state. Re-running after a
source-data or mapping change converges the tenant to the new desired values;
unchanged devices are effectively no-ops. This is the property that lets you run
writeback on a reconcile cadence (Guide 7).

**Next:** [Azure Arc server writeback](06-arc-server-writeback.qmd).
